name: Kep Beach and Town Center
tagline: The small central seafront where daily life gathers
description: The compact heart of Kep, strung along the small Kep Beach and the coastal road. Here you find the beach itself, a cluster of guesthouses and seaside restaurants, and easy access to swimming. It is the most convenient, walkable base for a first stay in town.
bestFor: First-timers and travellers who want to be near the beach and amenities
pros: Right by the beach and eateries
Good base for exploring the rest of Kep
cons: Can feel a touch busier on weekends and holidays
Limited nightlife and options after dark

name: Crab Market Area
tagline: Fresh seafood, pepper crab and working waterfront
description: A short way northwest of the beach, this is Kep's famous seafood strip, where the Crab Market sells just-caught crab cooked with Kampot pepper at open-air restaurants over the water. Boats to Koh Tonsay leave from nearby, making it a lively, food-focused corner of town.
bestFor: Seafood lovers and travellers who want to be near boats and eateries
pros: Boat departures to Rabbit Island nearby
cons: Busier and less peaceful than other areas
A few kilometres from the main beach

name: Kep National Park Hillside
tagline: Villas, viewpoints and the forested hiking loop
description: The green hillside rising behind the town, dotted with faded and ruined modernist villas and wrapped by the Kep National Park hiking loop. Guesthouses and bungalows here trade walkability for quiet, greenery and sweeping sea-and-hills views, a favourite for slow, nature-minded stays.
bestFor: Nature lovers and those wanting peace and views over convenience
cons: You need a scooter or tuktuk to get around
Further from restaurants and the beach

name: Koh Tonsay (Rabbit Island)
tagline: Offshore hammocks, sand and total slowdown
description: A small island a short boat ride offshore, reached from near the Crab Market. Rabbit Island offers simple beach bungalows, quiet sand and hammocks with minimal infrastructure and often patchy power and wifi. It is a rustic overnight escape rather than a practical work base.
bestFor: Travellers wanting a simple offline island night away from town
cons: Very basic infrastructure and unreliable power and wifi
